_doc: The case bank. TRIAGED 2026-07-28 against the rebuilt qualifying filter in knowledge/CASE_CRAFT.md. The filter added a HARD GATE that a case must have a disclosed cost class AND a disclosed decision-to-working timeline, because if we cannot tell the reader what it took, it is a story and not a plan. NONE of the 16 seeded cases carried a cost, and their 'timeline' fields held an announcement date rather than a duration, so all 16 were demoted from candidate to lead. They are not deleted: each carries a `qualification` block naming exactly which filter parts hold and exactly what a scout must go find, which is a far better starting point than an empty bank. Ship-ready count is 0, so the first run under the new contract triggers a full Phase 1 restock, which is the correct and honest state. Entries also predate the 2024-or-later recency rule and the 50-1000 employee band; both are recorded per entry. 2026-08-08 RESTOCK: wave 1 sent four scouts at four hunting grounds and returned ZERO qualifying cases and fifteen leads. Eight of the strongest are appended as bank-017 to bank-024. Every one died on the cost-and-timeline hard gate, not on the story. The convergent finding of all four scouts, and the most valuable thing the run produced: trade press reports outcomes and never asks what it ran, and cost gets said out loud only operator-to-operator (podcasts, independent newsletters, webinars, member forums, conference sessions). Literal cost-phrase searching is now dead craft and returns SEO spam. See out/2026-08-08/restock_notes.md for the full access map of 403ed hosts.

cases.size: 700 plus trucks, 650 plus drivers, family founded 1955
cases.bottleneck: Rising insurance costs, paper heavy back office, overdue preventive maintenance, no visibility into driver risk or trailer utilization.
cases.build: Samsara AI dash cams with automated driver coaching, telematics, driver app, smart trailer dormancy reports, plus an internal Fraley Score driver performance system built on top.

numbers.what: insurance cost reduction 2020 to 2023 while the market rose about 20 percent
back office admin savings, 99 percent less paperwork processing time
fewer overdue preventive maintenance checks
total estimated annual savings across programs

cases.skepticism: Vendor case study. The insurance number is the most concrete and externally anchored line. The rest are company estimates. Label vendor sourced.
cases.alaska_translation: Alaska trucking and air cargo run the same math with harsher roads and higher stakes. Insurance, maintenance compliance, and back office paperwork are universal fleet bottlenecks.
cases.notes: Strongest single company story in the bank for relatability. Alternates surfaced but not fetched, Halvor Lines (Netradyne), Dohrn Transfer (Samsara).

cases.build: OptimoRoute algorithmic route optimization with delivery time windows, unload times, and what if simulation for prospective customers.

numbers.what: fleet wide mileage reduction on 4.6 million annual miles
lower driver costs
more delivery capacity, about 330 extra deliveries a day, same fleet
on time rate improvement

cases.alaska_translation: Anchorage food and freight distribution runs the same static route trap. Percent level mileage cuts are real money at Alaska fuel and labor rates. Same math as the snowplow route studies.
cases.notes: Family produce house archetype. Pairs with the public sector plow route evidence for a boring optimization pays theme.

cases.size: About 1.5 million background checks a month for 100,000 plus businesses
cases.bottleneck: 2 percent of background check records are messy free text needing classification into 230 categories. GPT-4 hit 88 percent overall, 82 on hard cases, 7 to 15 second latency, 7,000 to 12,000 dollars a month.
cases.build: Fine tuned Llama-3 8B on their own data via Predibase, served on a single A100 GPU.

numbers.what: overall accuracy after fine tuning, 85 on the hardest cases
latency, roughly 30x faster
serving cost, roughly 5x cheaper than GPT-4

cases.skepticism: Original reporting by Computerworld with before and after baselines, though the underlying numbers are self reported by Checkr's ML engineer.
cases.alaska_translation: The cleanest public proof that a small model fine tuned on your own data can beat the big general model on cost, speed, and accuracy for one narrow job. The ownership story, your model, your data, costs that fall.
cases.notes: The model tuning capability file anchor. Over the size band as a tech firm, use for the mechanism with the size caveat said plainly.

cases.build: MachineMetrics tool monitoring, sensorless high frequency data from the machine control, ML detects imminent tool failure and feed holds the machine before it wrecks parts.

cases.notes: Small shop archetype, enabled lights out running.

cases.location: Oklahoma City, Oklahoma (plus Toronto and Cincinnati)
cases.size: around 250 employees, per the n8n case study page fetched 2026-08-08
cases.bottleneck: A government solicitation proposal took about two weeks of work from multiple contributors, solicitations regularly ran past 50 pages, and opportunities were missed entirely because thousands publish and nobody could read them all in time.
cases.build: Self-hosted n8n with a React/Node front end so business users could run it. Four workflows: proposal drafting against their own internal reference library, requirements extraction into a shall/must/will matrix, daily opportunity discovery via the Deltek GovWin API with scoring, and an internal chatbot over company data. Drafts are labelled AI-generated starting points and a human writes the last 20 percent.

numbers.value: two weeks of 3 to 4 people to about 25 minutes
numbers.what: time to an 80 percent proposal draft
consolidated shall/must/will requirements matrix per solicitation
annual software cost eliminated, two legacy tools replaced

cases.skepticism: Vendor page, no independent account found anywhere. Two named humans with real titles is unusually specific for a vendor page. The stat card and the quote disagree on the baseline (25 minutes vs 3-4 weeks, against Tatum's two weeks of three or four people); pin which. React/Node front end on self-hosted n8n needs a bought-vs-built test.
cases.alaska_translation: ANCSA subsidiaries and engineering firms running federal contracting practices feel this exact bottleneck every time a solicitation drops. P3 in DEPLOYMENT_PATTERNS.
cases.notes: THE STRONGEST LEAD OF THE 2026-08-08 RUN. Named humans Shawn Tatum (Senior Program Manager) and Jim Webster (CIO). Honest rung 4 that teaches the agent-washing lesson.

cases.size: over 100 employees, 25 trucks, family run by three family members, founded 1988
cases.bottleneck: The 3pm order cut-off. The CEO on the record: 'Before implementing Choco, I'd feel anxiety levels rise every day around 3pm as my team worked to manually key in bulk orders before a cut-off time, often facing poor reception and internal system outages.' Sales reps typed orders in their cars instead of selling.
cases.build: Bought Choco OrderAgent. Customers keep ordering the way they already order (email, text, photo of a handwritten list, voicemail); the system transcribes, parses, matches to SKUs and writes the order into the distributor's system. Exceptions go to a person.

numbers.what: reduction in order entry time
stated AI accuracy
